text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- Swiss atomic power plants in 1996 increased their total power production by 0.9 percent to 23.72 million megawatt hours. The share of atomic power of total electric energy production rose by four percent to 43 percent.
- The number of Swiss women who work rose to 62 percent from 49 percent between 1970 and 1990, a study of the Federal Office for Statistics wrote.
- Vontobel Bank Group reported a 46 percent rise in net profit to 60.2 million Swiss francs in 1996.
- Some 357 organs were transplanted in 1996. The waiting lists remain very long. Some 40 people died because of a shortage of organs.

- The Zurich airport registered a 5.8 percent rise in the number of passengers to 15.8 million in 1996. Geneva airport reported a 0.9 percent decline, which is due to Swissair's decision to withdraw most of its long-haul flights from Geneva to Zurich.
- Roche paid $1 billion for Tastemaker, a deal announced earlier this week in which the Swiss pharmaceuticals giant will purchase the American aroma producer.
- Swiss ombudsman for prices Werner Marti said that the banks should lower their mortgage rates.
- Swissair spun off its low-profit intercontinental holiday flight division to Charter Leisure. The new Swissair subsidiary is expected to generate profits by 1999.
- Swiss components maker Phoenix Mecano said it was expecting a 13 percent rise in 1996 net profit to 32 million Swiss francs.
